articles.title: Australia returns ancient stone heads to China after more than 30 years
articles.summary:
Australia has returned two stone sculptures to China after more than 30 years abroad.

The post Diesel prices may stay elevated into spring 2027, fuel executives warn  appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Diesel prices may stay elevated into spring 2027, fuel executives warn - FreightWaves JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — U.S. trucking companies could face elevated diesel prices through at least spring 2027, according to energy and truck stop executives speaking Tuesday at the WEX OTR Summit. Geopolitical conflicts, refinery constraints and limited pipeline capacity continue to strain fuel supplies could continue to impact the trucking industry, according to Chuck Ryan, president and CEO of AMBEST, a nationwide network of independent truck stops and service centers. Ryan said diesel prices are unlikely to decline significantly before spring, even if global crude oil prices retreat. “I don’t see it coming down until spring, and that’s if things start to work out on the war front,” Ryan told FreightWaves and Transport Topics during an interview following the panel discussion. Ryan said the ongoing conflicts involving Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine have disrupted global energy supplies, while U.S. refining and transportation infrastructure remains constrained. “If oil dropped today, that does not mean the price will go down,” Ryan said during the panel. “In fact, I think we will have this problem for the next several months, whether the wars end or not.” The discussion, titled “At the Pump & On the Margin: Navigating Fuel Price Volatility and Network Optimization,” featured executives from AMBEST, Circle K, Maverik and Dow Jones Energy. articles.content: Sanctioned Russian tankers head for US carrying diesel - Splash247 PTP LLC Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are heading towards the United States under the controversial agreement between presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, with Moscow preparing to dispatch a fourth vessel today. Russian deputy prime minister Alexander Novak confirmed yesterday that three shipments were underway, despite mounting opposition from US lawmakers who argue the deal breaches existing legislation prohibiting Russian energy imports. According to vessel tracking data from Kpler, the ships are Talisman, Leruo and Agioi Fanendes, carrying a combined 924,000 barrels of diesel. Two of the tankers are subject to international sanctions. The Talisman is sanctioned by the US and European Union, while Leruo appears on British and EU sanctions lists. The Malta-flagged Agioi Fanendes, managed by Greek interests, loaded approximately 40,000 tonnes of ultra-low sulphur diesel at Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22. The three ships departed Primorsk between October 16 and 22 and are expected to reach the US Atlantic coast between November 7 and 11, although their declared destinations remain subject to change. Novak said the shipments demonstrate that Moscow and Washington are implementing their agreement despite political opposition. articles.content: Port Houston container volumes jump 11% as imports surge in September - FreightWaves Port Houston recorded an 11% year-over-year increase in container volumes in September, fueled by stronger imports and improving export activity through its Bayport and Barbours Cut container terminals. The port handled 376,419 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) during the month, compared with 337,659 TEUs during the same month in 2025, according to figures presented during the Oct. 21 Port Commission meeting. Through the first nine months of 2026, Port Houston handled 3.35 million TEUs, up 2% from 3.27 million TEUs during the same period last year. Loaded container imports rose 16% year over year in September to 174,189 TEUs, while loaded exports increased 2% to 132,009 TEUs. Port Houston CEO Charlie Jenkins said September’s performance represented a significant improvement after a challenging start to 2026. “We had a pretty rough start to the year,” Jenkins told commissioners, adding that recent cargo activity had improved the port’s outlook heading into the final quarter. Ryan Mariacher, the port’s chief operations officer, said container activity at Bayport and Barbours Cut continued to benefit from stronger import demand, while export volumes began accelerating toward the end of September. “The growth at Bayport and Barber’s Cut for the month was largely driven by imports,” Mariacher said during the meeting. articles.content: Shipping's $275m lesson in the limits of sanctions screening - Splash247 Queen's College Oxford A sanctions settlement has exposed a fundamental weakness in shipping’s compliance systems. Wolfgang Lehmacher reports. On paper, Adani Enterprises did what compliance manuals demand. According to OFAC, before each LPG cargo arrived, it screened ships, operators and sellers against the US sanctions list. The names were clean. In May 2026, Adani agreed to pay $275m to settle OFAC’s case over 35 cargoes from a Dubai trader that OFAC says were Iranian. Among the red flags OFAC cites were AIS spoofing plus dark periods, illogical port calls, and frequent changes of name, owner and flag. Documents for Adani’s first cargo, fully refrigerated propane, said it was loaded at Sohar, in Oman. Sohar had no facilities at the time for exporting fully refrigerated LPG. In February 2024, the trader’s bank stopped payment for one shipment. The trader gave Adani a new account at another bank and supplied further shipping documents, which OFAC describes as apparently falsified. The payment went through. So did the cargoes. OFAC judged the case egregious: Adani had heard third-party concerns about Iranian origin four times, and its prices were, in OFAC’s view, not commercially reasonable. The warnings arrived in fragments. That is the core problem: the party carrying the liability rarely holds the whole evidence. Importers hold certificates of origin. articles.title: Millions in stolen freight reveal a weakness criminals keep exploiting
articles.summary:
From a $12 million cargo theft scheme to fraudulent shipment diversions, recent cases reveal a recurring weakness. The question is whether your team knows how to recognize it before freight moves.
The post Millions in stolen freight reveal a weakness criminals keep exploiting appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Millions in stolen freight reveal a weakness criminals keep exploiting - FreightWaves Recent freight fraud investigations have exposed millions of dollars in cargo losses across the United States. Federal prosecutors recently charged a driver in an alleged $12 million cargo theft conspiracy involving established trucking companies. A California trucking owner pleaded guilty in a separate $2.1 million identity theft case. Another investigation uncovered a nationwide cargo theft ring that purchased existing motor carriers to secure freight. Although these investigations involve different suspects, several reveal the same vulnerability within freight transportation. Criminals exploit legitimate business identities, established operating authorities, and trusted communications to gain control of shipments. Their tactics can make fraudulent transactions appear legitimate during routine carrier verification. The question is whether employees know what to verify before releasing freight. Established authority does not establish identity Federal prosecutors recently charged Nursulton Khaydarov in connection with an alleged cargo theft conspiracy exceeding $12 million. Investigators identified at least 24 shipments involving trucking companies that suspects allegedly purchased or controlled. articles.content: Zijin Mining orders bulker pair for African mineral trade - Splash247 Xinneng Shipbuilding Chinese mining giant Zijin Mining has returned to Shandong Xinneng Shipbuilding for two 3,000 dwt bulk carriers, expanding its dedicated mineral transport operation on Lake Tanganyika in eastern Africa. The latest contract follows an earlier order for four 2,000 dwt vessels at the same Chinese yard, which are now operating on the lake between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania. The new ships will be 50% larger than their predecessors, adding a combined 6,000 dwt to Zijin’s lake transport capacity. Contract value and delivery dates have not been disclosed. The investment forms part of Zijin’s efforts to establish an alternative export corridor for minerals from its operations in the DRC. The group’s existing shipping operation links Congolese cargoes with Kigoma in Tanzania, from where they can move towards the country’s Indian Ocean export infrastructure. Zijin’s first four lake bulkers were built through an arrangement that saw hull sections manufactured in China and assembled in Tanzania, overcoming the logistical challenges of building vessels for an African inland waterway. The company established the route to support its growing mining interests in central Africa and reduce dependence on existing overland transport connections. articles.content: US moves to extend China ship fee truce into 2027 - Splash247 Port of Long Beach The United States is looking to extend its suspension of additional port fees targeting China-linked shipping for another two months, keeping the measures on hold until January 9, 2027, while trade negotiations with Beijing continue. The Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) has opened a public consultation on a proposal to prolong the suspension from November 10, when the current arrangement expires. Under the proposed extension, operators would continue to be exempt from the additional maritime transport charges introduced under Washington’s Section 301 investigation into China’s dominance of shipping, logistics and shipbuilding. The proposal would also maintain the suspension of separate duties on certain cargo-handling equipment. The US initially introduced the vessel charges in October 2025, targeting Chinese-owned and operated ships, Chinese-built tonnage operated by non-Chinese companies and certain foreign-built vehicle carriers. The measures prompted widespread changes to fleet deployment plans, with owners and operators looking to limit their exposure to the additional costs. articles.content: First look: Covenant Logistics’ Q3 freight revenue surges 68% - FreightWaves Covenant Logistics Group reported a 19.2% year-over-year increase in third-quarter revenue Thursday, driven by strong growth in its managed freight segment. The Chattanooga, Tennessee-based carrier (NYSE: CVLG) generated $353.9 million in total revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with $296.9 million a year earlier. Freight revenue excluding fuel surcharges rose 17.2% to $315.1 million from $268.8 million. Other highlights during the quarter included improved freight pricing, even as the trucking company continued shrinking its tractor fleet and shifting capacity toward long-term contracts. Net income increased to $10.7 million, or 40 cents per diluted share, compared with $9.1 million, or 35 cents per share, in the third quarter of 2025. On an adjusted basis, Covenant earned 50 cents per diluted share, up 13.6% from 44 cents a year earlier. Chairman and CEO David R. Parker said the results marked the first time since the second quarter of 2022 that adjusted earnings per share increased both sequentially and year over year. “We were pleased with our third-quarter earnings of $0.40 per diluted share, or $0.50 per diluted share on a non-GAAP adjusted basis,” Parker said in a news release. The company’s operating income increased to $12.5 million from $7.9 million a year earlier. articles.content: Saia’s expanded terminal network delivers record revenue, tonnage - FreightWaves Less-than-truckload carrier Saia continued to see outsized volume growth in the third quarter as it leveraged an expanded terminal network. The period delivered record revenue and tonnage for the company, with its focus now centered on improving operating results at the new locations. Saia’s (NASDAQ: SAIA) reported third-quarter earnings per share of $3.41 on Thursday before the market opened. The result was 60 cents higher y/y and 11 cents better than the consensus estimate. A $3.6-million decline in net interest expense was a 10-cent y/y tailwind. (The comparison to the 2025 third quarter excludes a $14.5-million net impact from real estate gains and impairments, resulting in adjusted EPS of $2.81.) Revenue of $983 million was 17% higher y/y and $15 million better than analysts’ expectations. (Diesel prices were 48% higher y/y in the quarter.) Tonnage was up 9% y/y as shipments increased 1% and weight per shipment grew 8%. On a y/y comparison, tonnage increased 7.8% in July, 8.7% in August and 10.3% in September. Tonnage is up 10% y/y so far in October. Since 2022, the company has opened 45 new terminals and relocated or expanded another 25. articles.content: Korean carrier Namsung returns to China for larger boxships - Splash247 Namsung South Korea’s Namsung Shipping has been linked to another containership order in China, with brokers reporting a deal for two firm 7,100 teu vessels at Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Corporation (DSIC), plus options for another pair. Shipbroking sources said the CSSC-owned yard had secured the contract, with deliveries expected between 2030 and 2031. No price or propulsion specifications have been disclosed. The reported agreement would mark Namsung’s first order at DSIC and its second shipbuilding deal in China this year. The Seoul-based carrier entered the Chinese newbuilding market in March, booking two 4,300 teu containerships at CSSC’s Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. The order formed part of a wider four-vessel agreement also involving fellow South Korean operator Dongyoung Shipping, which contracted two 1,900 teu feeders. Namsung’s latest reported 7,100 teu contract represents a significant increase in vessel size from that earlier order. The carrier, established in 1953, operates primarily across intra-Asian liner trades linking South Korea, Japan, China and Southeast Asia. Its current company website identifies 20 operating vessels, with its network extending across multiple regional services. DSIC has meanwhile built up a substantial commercial orderbook across crude and product tankers, shuttle tankers, bulk carriers and containerships. articles.content: CPKC reports record revenue on strength of grain and intermodal traffic - FreightWaves CPKC reported stronger third-quarter operating income Wednesday, on record revenue and higher volumes. “Against a pretty dynamic backdrop, I’m pleased with what the team has delivered,” Chief Executive Keith Creel said on an earnings call after the close of markets.“We handled 6% more volume while continuing to improve the performance of the railroad, and more importantly, there is so much more opportunity in front of us.” Quarterly operating income rose 11%, to $1.06 billion U.S., as revenue increased 15%, to $3 billion. Earnings per share grew 3%, to 74 cents. The improved performance didn’t extend to the operating ratio, a key indicator of efficiency. The OR was 64.8%, a 1.3-point increase over a year ago as expenses climbed 18% largely due to higher fuel costs. Volume was up 5% when measured by carloads and containers, or 6% on the basis of revenue ton-miles, which is CPKC’s preferred metric. The Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP) set records for domestic and international intermodal volumes, as well as for grain. Grain carloads were up 20%, intermodal was up 9%, and metals, minerals, and consumer products traffic grew 8%. Potash and coal volume each declined 8%. Potash shipments were curtailed due to maintenance at port loading facilities, while mine production issues suppressed coal volume. articles.content: India greenlights $1bn drive to break China's container manufacturing dominance - Splash247 LR India has approved a INR100bn ($1.05bn) programme to massively expand domestic shipping container manufacturing, targeting a tenfold increase in annual capacity as New Delhi seeks to challenge China’s near-monopoly over the industry. The country’s cabinet approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme yesterday, turning a proposal announced in February’s national budget into a 13-year industrial development programme. The initiative aims to increase India’s annual container manufacturing capacity from approximately 70,000 teu today to 750,000 teu, potentially establishing the country as a significant international supplier of shipping containers. Chinese manufacturers currently account for more than 95% of global dry freight container production and virtually the entire refrigerated container market. India hopes to erode that dominance through a combination of production subsidies, subsidised financing and investment in manufacturing infrastructure. The programme includes INR88.91bn in financial assistance for containers manufactured to international standards, alongside INR8.59bn in support for financing new factories and expanding existing production facilities. Manufacturers will be eligible for a 3% annual interest subsidy on qualifying loans. articles.content: VLCC delivery wave set to reach levels not seen since the 1970s - Splash247 Hengli Group The VLCC sector is heading for its biggest delivery wave in half a century, with more than 100 new supertankers scheduled to enter service annually in both 2028 and 2029, according to Hartland Shipping Services. The scale recalls the supertanker boom of the 1970s. BIMCO’s historical figures put the all-time record at 116 VLCCs delivered in 1974. Since then, even the 68 deliveries recorded in 2019 represented a four-decade high. The historical precedent is worth noting. A wave of tankers ordered during the early 1970s boom arrived just as the 1973 oil shock devastated demand. Between 1974 and 1975, global oil trade plunged 23% while tanker capacity grew nearly 16%, according to UNCTAD. Freight rates collapsed. The reopening of the Suez Canal in 1975 further shortened voyages. By year-end, 573 tankers representing 47.8m dwt were laid up, according to INTERTANKO. Owners faced financial ruin, newbuildings went straight into lay-up and the industry endured a prolonged depression. Hartland now counts 319 VLCCs on order, equivalent to 34% of the existing fleet, rising to 42% when sanctioned ships are excluded. Yet just 20 are scheduled for delivery over the next six months. Only six VLCCs delivered last year and just one in 2024. This could be an upcoming supply disaster Of the current orderbook, 138 ships are not due until 2029 or later. articles.content: Trader Alkagesta enters shipowning with Turkish bunker fleet takeover - Splash247 Energy Petrol Malta-based commodities trader Alkagesta is entering shipowning through the acquisition of Turkish marine fuel supplier Energy Petrol, taking over an eight-vessel bunker fleet as it expands its physical fuel distribution business. The Orkhan Rustamov-led company confirmed on October 22 that it had agreed to acquire the Istanbul-based supplier in a transaction already approved by Türkiye’s competition authority. Financial terms have not been disclosed, and Energy Petrol is expected to continue operating independently. The deal marks Alkagesta’s first investment in owned vessels, moving the group beyond fuel trading and chartered shipping into direct physical distribution. Energy Petrol, established in 1997 by Mustafa and Yeşim Muhtaroğlu, is an established bunker supplier in the Turkish Straits region. The company operates bunker tankers supplying marine gasoil and fuel oil, with its fleet including the 3,659 dwt Deniz M, the 2,818 dwt Energy K and smaller vessels serving the Istanbul market. Energy Petrol’s website lists a wider historical fleet, although the companies have not identified which eight vessels are included in the transaction. Alkagesta estimates that it already supplies approximately 40% of Turkey’s annual 2.5m-tonne marine fuel market and around 75% of Malta’s bunkering market. articles.content: Swedish owner Veritas books up to six chemical tankers in China - Splash247 Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment Swedish shipowner Veritas Tankers has placed an order for up to six 13,000 dwt stainless steel chemical tankers at China’s Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment, in a deal potentially worth $248m. The yard’s Shenzhen-listed parent, Jiangsu Rainbow Heavy Industries, confirmed the contract with an unnamed European owner in a stock exchange filing, putting the total value of the six-ship package, including options, at CNY1.5bn to CNY1.65bn ($225m to $248m). Shipbroking sources identify Sweden’s Rederi AB Veritas Tankers as the buyer, although the shipowner has not publicly confirmed its involvement. Rainbow has withheld the customer’s identity on commercial confidentiality grounds. The Chinese group has not specified how many vessels are firm and how many remain optional, but said deliveries are scheduled to begin 28 months after the contract is signed. The newbuildings are intended for parcel chemical trades, with designs suited to restricted waterways and operating conditions in northern Europe. For Rainbow, the deal adds another European customer to its chemical tanker business. The Nantong yard previously secured a contract from Germany’s John T. articles.content: Evalend drops newcastlemax option at Dajin Heavy - Splash247 Greek shipowner Evalend Shipping has been linked to the decision not to exercise an option for a fourth 211,000 dwt newcastlemax bulker at China’s Dajin Heavy Industry, removing a potential CNY525m ($78m) vessel from the yard’s order pipeline. Dajin disclosed that the option under a three-plus-one shipbuilding agreement signed in July had expired and that the Greek customer had elected not to proceed after discussions between the parties. The three firm ships, valued at a combined CNY1.575bn (about $235m), remain on order at subsidiary Tangshan Dajin, with completion scheduled across 2029 and 2030. The original deal carried a maximum value of CNY2.1bn ($313m) if the additional ship was declared. The yard said the decision does not constitute a contractual breach or trigger penalties. Dajin also expects no material impact on its production schedule or 2026 financial performance. The Chinese group did not identify the customer in its filing. However, Chinese shipbuilding market reports have linked the contract to Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend Shipping. Splash covered the original agreement in July when Evalend emerged as the reported buyer of the three-plus-one series, marking the Greek owner’s entry into the newcastlemax sector. articles.content: China Merchants tanker arm targets Yangtze fleet renewal - Splash247 China Merchants-controlled Nanjing Tanker is planning to invest up to RMB191.72m ($28.7m) in ten 4,000 dwt crude oil barges as it moves to upgrade its fleet serving refineries along the Yangtze River. The Shanghai-listed owner has approved the investment through wholly owned subsidiary Nanjing Yangtze River Oil Transport Logistics, with Hunan Jinhang Shipbuilding selected to construct the vessels. The barges will be fitted with cargo oil pumps to support self-unloading operations, responding to demand from petrochemical and refinery customers along the waterway. Construction is scheduled to proceed in batches through 2027, according to the company’s filing. The project received unanimous board approval but still requires shareholder consent before proceeding. Nanjing Tanker operates across domestic coastal, river and international oil transportation markets. The China Merchants Group-controlled company has a fleet of more than 70 vessels, including crude and product tankers. The proposed barges form a separate investment from the company’s recently disclosed LR2 tanker expansion at Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Corporation. That four-vessel, methanol-ready LR2 programme was previously reported by Splash. articles.content: New Drewry data shows import demand boosting trans-Pacific rates - FreightWaves Ends Friday 10/23 F3 Promo code: LUCKYLAST50 Register → × Drewry’s World Container Index rose 2% to $4,585 per 40-foot container, supported by higher rates on trans-Pacific and Asia-Europe routes as strong U.S. import demand and carrier capacity cuts bolstered pricing. Shanghai-to-Los Angeles rates increased 2% to $8,007 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-to-New York rates edged up 1% to $10,166. Drewry expects trans-Pacific rates to remain stable next week, with U.S. import demand continuing to support the market despite an increase in available capacity. Carriers have announced only two blank sailings on the trans-Pacific for next week, down from six this week, according to figures from Drewry’s Container Capacity Insight. The service tracks scheduled and canceled sailings, effective capacity and port congestion across major trade lanes. Rates from Shanghai to Rotterdam rose 3% to $3,632 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-to-Genoa rates increased 5% to $4,152. Unlike the trans-Pacific, the Asia-Europe trade faces more sailing cancellations next week. Carriers have announced eight blank sailings, up from two this week, tightening available capacity as they seek to put upward pressure on freight rates. articles.summary:

The post Workforce gaps keep supply chain AI stuck in pilot mode appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Workforce gaps keep supply chain AI stuck in pilot mode - FreightWaves Ends Friday 10/23 F3 Promo code: LUCKYLAST50 Register → × Freight technology vendors are selling AI agents that can benchmark rates and award freight under rules a customer sets. A new survey finds most supply chain organizations still limit AI to generating insights, and the first obstacle the research names is their own workforce. The Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM) and the Digital Supply Chain Institute (DSCI) released The People Paradox in Supply Chain AI Integration on Oct. 14. Of the supply chain professionals surveyed, 83% said their employees are unprepared to use AI effectively. The 17% who described their workforce as ready reported a 71% AI project success rate. Everyone else reported 28%, and about 64% of that group is still in the pilot or planning stage. Abe Eshkenazi, CEO of ASCM, said most AI sessions at supply chain conferences run through the same agenda: the challenges, the implementation, and the benefits. Every one of them ends with a reminder not to forget about the people, he said. “It’s interesting because from our perspective that’s where you ought to start the conversation,” Eshkenazi told FreightWaves. AI mostly stays in planning The report scored AI adoption across 13 core supply chain functions on a scale from 1, meaning no AI use, to 5, meaning autonomous execution without human review.
